query: What open-response signals predict low learning satisfaction?

per_column.name: instructional_pacing_issue
per_column.rationale: Pacing problems (too fast/slow) are a plausible driver of satisfaction extracted from the open response, external to the rating itself.

per_column.name: asynchronous_content_benefit
per_column.rationale: Format affordance (reusable/rewatchable vs livestream-only) is a course attribute that could shape satisfaction without restating it.

per_column.name: hands_on_or_lab_gap
per_column.rationale: Missing critical lab work is a structural gap plausibly predictive of low satisfaction, distinct from the score.

per_column.name: peer_interaction_quality
per_column.rationale: Quality of peer collaboration is a legitimate experiential predictor of satisfaction, not a component of the rating.

per_column.name: teacher_feedback_responsiveness
per_column.rationale: Feedback timeliness/quality is an external instructional variable with clear predictive signal for satisfaction.

per_column.name: subject_remote_format_fit
per_column.rationale: How well the subject suits remote delivery is a contextual predictor lying outside the satisfaction score.

per_column.name: emotional_affect_during_class
per_column.rationale: Affect (joyful/energized vs distressed_crying) is near-synonymous with satisfaction; it is an affective restatement of the outcome measured from the same response, so it leaks rather than predicts.

per_column.name: curiosity_and_intrinsic_motivation_trajectory
per_column.rationale: Motivation trajectory is conceptually distinct from a satisfaction rating and can plausibly serve as a correlated but non-identical predictor, though it borders on affective overlap.

judge.rationale: Most added columns are content-derived experiential features (pacing, format, labs, peer interaction, feedback, subject fit) that lie outside the satisfaction score and carry genuine predictive signal, giving the set substantial leverage beyond the original columns. One column (emotional_affect_during_class) essentially restates the outcome as affect and constitutes leakage, and the motivation trajectory column borders on affective overlap; excluding the leaking feature, the remaining set still provides strong, non-redundant predictive value.
